cand.title: OHBM 2027 Annual Meeting
cand.excerpt: Strong organized hospitality-demand mechanism and confirmed Toronto date; venue commitment reduces current-edition accessibility.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Primary routing contact: Emily Weber, Senior Meetings & Education Manager, eweber@humanbrainmapping.org; OHBM assigns Annual Meeting operations and future-hosting enquiries to her. Executive escalation: Beth Slater, Executive Director, bslater@humanbrainmapping.org, identified as Elizabeth Slater in the 2027 FAQ. Katie Johnson, Senior Partnership Engagement & Operations Manager, kjohnson@humanbrainmapping.org, is relevant for sponsorship/exhibitor pathways, not a verified housing buyer. Jean Chen and Rosanna Olsen are Toronto local organizing stakeholders, not verified purchasing authorities. Older generic OHBM specifications state that contracts are negotiated and signed by the Executive Director; this is published general policy, not evidence that any particular 2027 hotel contract exists.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced activity dates: June 26–30, 2027, Metro Toronto Convention Centre, Toronto, Canada. These are meeting dates, not publication dates, and are within the requested horizon. Registration is scheduled to open January 2027. The subsequent announced edition is June 18–22, 2028, PACIFICO Yokohama, Yokohama, Japan; it is not a Toronto lodging opportunity.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specifications: this is a downtown convention-support opportunity, not a resort retreat. Expected congress scale is 3,500 delegates according to the August 11, 2026 Leaders Circle bid article; a 157-room hotel cannot be exclusive housing or replace MTCC. Plausible roles are a bounded delegate/speaker/organizer lodging allocation, self-booking attendees, VIP stays, or small side meetings. An exploratory 15–109 peak-room offer would be a hotel sales scenario only, not published event demand. The supplied Harbourfront location and walkability to MTCC support consideration, but no capture share is established. The supplied largest room, approximately 240 theatre, cannot host the plenary. Do not promise receptions or catering until current restaurant/lounge and banquet-service capabilities are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: OHBM explicitly names Metro Toronto Convention Centre, 255 Front St W, Toronto, Ontario M5V 2W6, Canada, in downtown Toronto proper and inside the hotel’s downtown/MTCC territory. It is a convention centre, not an incumbent competing hotel. This is a published venue commitment; a signed venue contract, allocated building and contracted hotel inventory were not disclosed in the reviewed materials.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified international annual series: Montréal 2023; Seoul 2024; Brisbane 2025; Bordeaux 2026; Toronto 2027; Yokohama 2028. OHBM states Toronto 2027 is its return after 22 years, the previous Toronto meeting being 2005. Recurrence of the series is verified, but annual Toronto recurrence is not. Historical edition details are separated below.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2027-specific sourcing remains unknown: no named official hotel, host hotel, hotel list, published block, housing bureau, housing booking portal or open Toronto hotel RFP was identified in the reviewed official 2027 materials. Accordingly, there are no verified 2027 hotels to name; this does not mean no hotels have been contracted. Source quotation for the established commitment: “Join us for the OHBM 2027 Annual Meeting, taking place June 26 - June 30, 2027, at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre in Toronto, Canada.” Important contextual distinction: the separate OHBM 2030 RFP, proposals due September 11, 2026, says “OHBM is not seeking a traditional attendee guest room block for this meeting” and requests “Approximately 10–15 guestrooms for OHBM staff, award recipients and other designated VIPs.” It also says “No attendee room block or attrition commitment is anticipated as part of this RFP.” These are 2030 requirements, not Toronto 2027 room demand or booking commitments. The older generic specifications call for a host hotel and overflow hotels; neither document establishes a Toronto incumbent or an open 2027 solicitation.
findings.organizationStructure: Event owner is Organization for Human Brain Mapping, an international scientific society with member-led committees and a globally rotating Annual Meeting. The 2030 RFP explicitly states “OHBM is managed by Global Management Partners,” a full-service association management company, and says its listed meeting contact is employed by that company and assigned to OHBM. Thus the supported model is association owner plus AMC operations, not a corporate-owned conference or a hotel-owned event. MTCC is the announced venue. No separate Toronto housing bureau, PCO or DMC appointment was verified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The main meeting venue is already announced, so this is not an opportunity to replace the congress venue. No named Toronto incumbent lodging hotel, contracted block, sell-out, pickup report, unmet room demand or actual overflow shortfall was verified. OHBM’s older generic overflow-hotel requirement is not proof of Toronto 2027 overflow. The September 2026-due 2030 RFP describes budget-sensitive attendees independently booking hotels and alternative accommodation, a material warning against assuming centralized mass room-block demand; applying that model to 2027 would remain an inference.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Emily Weber first, copying Beth Slater only as appropriate. Ask whether Toronto 2027 follows independent attendee booking, whether a host/VIP hotel has been selected, whether a housing bureau is involved, and whether additional hotels can join an official courtesy list or supply a small room allocation. Reference the 157-room Harbourfront hotel and MTCC access from the supplied brief; offer a bounded inventory/rate discussion only after confirming the sourcing route. Ask for actual dates including setup/shoulder nights, rooms by night, rate band, cutoff, concessions and contracting party before quoting. Use Katie Johnson only for exhibitor/sponsor introductions. Check hotel availability and food-service capability before proposing ancillary meetings or receptions. Monitor January 2027 registration materials if housing information is not yet released.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: As of November 15, 2026: the 2027 edition is upcoming and its convention venue is confirmed; lodging accessibility is unconfirmed. The prior likely_closed_incumbent label is not substantiated for hotels by the reviewed evidence. Do not mark hotel sourcing open or committed elsewhere. Pursue a permission-based housing-policy enquiry rather than an unsolicited claim of available official overflow. January 2027 registration opening is a published monitoring milestone, not a hotel-sourcing deadline.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: build the organizer relationship now for any genuinely available 2027 small host/VIP allocation, courtesy accommodation listing, or later room-availability need. There is no sourced evidence of a lost incumbent block that can be competitively displaced. The next edition, June 18–22, 2028 in Yokohama, provides no direct Toronto room demand. Toronto last hosted in 2005; no subsequent Toronto return date is verified. The separate 2030 Americas RFP is outside the requested horizon and must not be presented as a Toronto 2027 hotel RFP or proof of a future Toronto return.
